Report_ID: Cerebral palsy, any severity, at minimum 18 months corrected age
Title: Antenatal magnesium sulphate for the prevention of cerebral palsy in infants born preterm: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, multi-centre trial
Author: Wolf HT, et al. (MASP research group)
Comment: Paper reports an adjusted odds ratio, not a risk ratio; raw counts extracted for RR pooling. Denominators 343/337 are foetuses/children included in the primary (ITT) analysis (all randomised children), not only the 321/313 surviving children assessed. This row overlaps with the moderate-to-severe CP row (E1) from the same children; use only one in a pooled analysis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Antenatal magnesium sulphate (5 g loading dose, then 1 g/hour)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: pregnant women at imminent risk of preterm delivery before 32 weeks of gestation and their children
Outcome measurement: Number of children diagnosed with cerebral palsy of any severity out of foetuses/children included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis (343 MgSO4 vs 337 placebo; i.e. all randomised children)
Outcome variable: Cerebral palsy, any severity, at minimum 18 months corrected age
unit_of_analysis: per child (foetuses/children in ITT analysis = all randomised children)
reported_effect_measure: adjusted odds ratio (adjusted for plurality and gestational age at randomisation)

Report_ID: Cerebral palsy at 2 years' corrected age
Title: Prenatal Intravenous Magnesium at 30-34 Weeks' Gestation and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Offspring: The MAGENTA Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Crowther et al.
Comment: Unadjusted RR 0.98 (0.43-2.25) recorded as the ratio matching the raw counts; the paper also reports an adjusted RR 0.98 (0.43-2.23) adjusted for hospital site, gestational age at entry, and plurality. Denominator is children with cerebral palsy data assessed at 2 years, not all live births or all randomised infants.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intravenous magnesium sulfate 4 g over 30 minutes') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Children born to pregnant individuals at risk of imminent preterm birth at 30-34 weeks' gestation
Recruitment source: 24 Australian and New Zealand maternity hospitals, January 2012 to April 2018
Outcome measurement: Number of children with cerebral palsy out of children with cerebral palsy data assessed at 2 years' corrected age (denominator = children with data on cerebral palsy: 679 magnesium, 667 placebo)
Outcome variable: Cerebral palsy at 2 years' corrected age
unit_of_analysis: per child with cerebral palsy data at 2 years' corrected age

Report_ID: Cerebral palsy at a corrected age of 2 years
Title: Effect of Magnesium Sulfate Given for Neuroprotection Before Preterm Birth: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Crowther CA, Hiller JE, Doyle LW, Haslam RR (ACTOMgSO4 Collaborative Group)
Comment: Table 2 percentages (6.8%, 8.2%) are computed on children with cerebral palsy data; the Table 2 column headers list infants alive at randomization (629 vs 626). Denominators of 533 and 513 were taken from Table 5 'Severity of cerebral palsy - No. of children with data', which reproduce the reported percentages (36/533 = 6.8%; 42/513 = 8.2%). RR was estimated by log binomial regression with robust variance for clustering within mothers, not Mantel-Haenszel.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Magnesium sulfate (antenatal, for neuroprotection)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women with fetuses <30 weeks' gestation for whom birth was planned or expected within 24 hours, and their children
Recruitment source: 16 tertiary hospitals with neonatal intensive care units (13 Australia, 3 New Zealand), February 1996 - September 2000
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of children diagnosed with cerebral palsy among children with 2-year corrected age cerebral palsy data (533 magnesium sulfate vs 513 placebo; 14 children without assessments excluded as missing data)
Outcome variable: Cerebral palsy at a corrected age of 2 years
unit_of_analysis: per child with 2-year cerebral palsy data

Report_ID: Cerebral palsy at 18 corrected months of age
Title: Association between the use of antenatal magnesium sulfate in preterm labor and adverse health outcomes in infants (MagNET Trial)
Author: Mittendorf R, Dambrosia J, Pryde PG, Lee KS, Gianopoulos JG, Besinger RE, Tomich PG
Comment: No statistical test was reported for cerebral palsy ("our study was too small and the complication of cerebral palsy was too uncommon for meaningful statistical analysis"); only event counts are available. Denominators are all infants in each arm (30 vs 29), not an explicitly reported number assessed at 18 months. Table VII appears to list only 2 preventive cases exposed to 4 g MgSO4 plus 1 "not given", which conflicts with the narrative/Comment counts of 3 vs 0; the narrative counts were used.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Single 4-g intravenous MgSO4 bolus (preventive/neuroprotective dose)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women in preterm labor at >24 to <34 completed weeks with cervical dilatation >4 cm (poor tocolysis candidates) and their infants
Recruitment source: Hospital admissions, University of Chicago-affiliated centers, October 1995 - January 1997
Outcome measurement: Number of infants diagnosed with cerebral palsy out of infants randomized/born in each arm of the doubly masked preventive trial (denominator = all infants in that arm, 30 vs 29; the paper does not give a separate number assessed at 18 months)
Outcome variable: Cerebral palsy at 18 corrected months of age
unit_of_analysis: per infant (all infants in each arm; no separate number assessed reported)

Report_ID: Cerebral palsy at 2 years of corrected age (any severity; number of children diagnosed)
Title: A Randomized, Controlled Trial of Magnesium Sulfate for the Prevention of Cerebral Palsy
Author: Rouse et al.
Comment: Events are CHILDREN (41 and 74) but the denominators the paper gives in this sentence are PREGNANCIES with a 2-year CP assessment (942 and 1002); the paper does not give a child-level denominator for this outcome. No risk ratio or CI is reported for this any-severity child-level outcome (only P=0.004).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Magnesium sulfate (6-g IV bolus then 2 g/hr infusion)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women at 24-31 weeks of gestation at imminent risk for preterm delivery (singletons or twins) and their children
Recruitment source: 20 NICHD Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network clinical sites, USA, Dec 1997 - May 2004
Outcome measurement: Number of children with a diagnosis of cerebral palsy; denominator reported by the paper is pregnancies with a 2-year cerebral palsy assessment (942 magnesium, 1002 placebo)
Outcome variable: Cerebral palsy at 2 years of corrected age (any severity; number of children diagnosed)
unit_of_analysis: children with CP counted against pregnancies with a 2-year CP assessment (paper's own denominator)
